verdict.rationale: Modal's pricing page says users never pay for idle resources and are billed only for actual compute time "by the CPU cycle", which implies granularity finer than per-second. Supporting claims say containers spin up and down in 1-2 seconds and endpoints idle at zero, which reinforces billing only while running. missing for 10: an explicit statement of the billing unit (per-second or per-minute) or a published rate table, details on how container idle timeouts are billed, and independent or hands-on corroboration of actual invoices.

support.subject: As an ML engineer, I am billed at per-second or per-minute granularity and only while my instance is actually running

citations.quote: You never pay for idle resources — just actual compute time, by the CPU cycle.
Turn any function into an HTTPS endpoint that scales with traffic and idles at zero.
In contrast, _Modal spins containers_ up and down in 1-2 seconds.
